scenario.name: competing-flow-bulk-capped
scenario.description: The capped half of the egress ceiling's competitor pair (#481): scenario 22 with upload.max_egress_bytes_per_second set to 256 KiB/s - about 2.1 Mbit/s of request-body bytes, 21% of the 10 Mbit/s bottleneck - and nothing else changed. The number to read is competitor_goodput_mbps_with beside scenario 22's, each against its own solo windows. Per-cycle engine (process-once): the competitor refuses engine_mode run by design, so each cycle's fresh engine starts with a full bucket of R/32. Requires the netem stack, docker compose -f benchmarks/docker-compose.benchmark.yml --profile netem --profile containerized up -d.

competitor.competitor_window_unaccounted_is: the flow's wall clock its own report does not describe — docker's startup and the TCP connect before iperf3 began measuring, its closing exchange and exit after it stopped. A cost of the plumbing, not an uncertainty in where the window sat
competitor.competitor_window_placed_by: the instant each interval line of iperf3's --json-stream was written, stamped beside iperf3 in the probe container, less where that interval ends on the window's own clock; the earliest such estimate is taken, so the placement is late by at most the fastest line's write. The report's final line is left out: iperf3 writes it only after its end-of-test exchange with the server, across the shaped link, and competitor_window_final_line_delay_seconds is how much later it was. competitor_window_setup_seconds is how much of the unaccounted overhead fell before the window opened; competitor_window_sync_spread_seconds is how far the other lines' estimates disagreed, refused above 0.25s as a stream that was not read live
competitor.vtop_goodput_is: committed object bytes; excludes framing, manifests, retries
competitor.vtop_window_is: the span from the first attributed engine cycle's start to the last one's return; cycles straddling either edge of the competitor's window are excluded because their bytes cannot be split, so this is nested inside the competitor's window rather than equal to it. BOTH of the index's rates are taken over this span
competitor.competitor_goodput_over_vtop_window_is: the receiver's byte total for the window, spread across it in the proportion the report's own per-second stream gives and restricted to vtop_window_seconds; the stream is the sender's, so it supplies the shape only and never the magnitude

network_counters_withheld: host-wide counters include the competing flow inside the engine's window
bottleneck_observations: The competing flow kept 81.27% of its solo goodput while the engine ran (7.759 vs 9.547 Mbit/s). Over the 37.296s the index is taken on it held 7.469 Mbit/s against VTOP's 1.741 (Jain 0.7211). Low compression ratio — data may be high-entropy or already compressed.
